# Agentic On-Call RCA: Resolve Incidents 9× Faster


- [September 14, 2026](https://struct.ai/articles/2026/09/14/)


*Written by: Nimesh Chakravarthi, Co-founder & CTO, Struct*


## Key Takeaways for Agentic On-Call RCA


- Agentic on-call root cause analysis uses a six-stage observe-hypothesize-query-evaluate-verify-report workflow that cuts manual triage from 45 minutes to 5 minutes.
- Manual investigation forces context-switching across five or more disconnected tools, while agentic flows remove those handoffs by automating observation, hypothesis generation, and verification.
- The architecture combines LangGraph orchestration, MCP tool interfaces, parallel hypothesis management, and a dedicated verifier agent to create an auditable evidence trail.
- Human escalation gates separate investigation from remediation, so junior engineers can participate safely while explicit approval is still required before any fix runs.
- Teams like Arcana reclaim 56 engineer-hours per month with 85–90% helpful investigations;[see how Struct automates your on-call workflow](https://cal.com/deepanm/struct-demo) and aim for similar results.


## Why Manual Triage Takes 45 Minutes While Agentic Flows Take 5


Manual triage takes 45 minutes because engineers must context-switch across five or more disconnected tools, often while half-asleep and under SLA pressure. They acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty, open Datadog to inspect metrics, pivot to Sentry for exception details, query CloudWatch for raw logs, and cross-reference GitHub for recent deploys.[A 2024 study by Roy et al. on cloud incident RCA describes root cause analysis as a demanding task for on-call engineers who must manually correlate fragmented signals from logs, metrics, traces, deploy history, and ownership data.](https://augmentcode.com/guides/root-cause-analysis-ai-agents) Each handoff between tools adds minutes, and the cognitive overhead of rebuilding context from scratch adds more.


An agentic RCA workflow removes those manual handoffs. The moment an alert fires, the system begins observation automatically. By the time an engineer opens their laptop, hypothesis generation, evidence gathering, and initial verification already run to completion.[Customer Arcana cut investigation time from 30 minutes to 2 minutes and reclaims 56 engineer-hours per month.](https://struct.ai/case-study/arcana) That 80% reduction in triage time is a measured outcome from a production deployment running 2,100+ automated investigations monthly.


[Connect your integrations and automate triage](https://cal.com/deepanm/struct-demo) , then let agentic RCA handle the next alert before you reach for your laptop.


## The Observe-Hypothesize-Query-Evaluate-Verify-Report Workflow


That 5-minute investigation time comes from a specific six-stage workflow that removes the manual handoffs described above. The sequence maps directly to how expert SREs reason during live incidents, while running in parallel and at machine speed.[The RCA loop in incident agents follows an iterative sequence of Observe, Hypothesize, Test, Narrow, and Rank, surfacing the most likely cause only when confidence is sufficient.](https://augmentcode.com/guides/ai-agents-incident-management)


1. **Observe:** The alert fires and the agent immediately ingests the incident timeline, linked telemetry, blast radius, and service topology.[Inputs include metrics from Prometheus or Datadog (anomaly window plus 30–60 minutes of baseline), structured logs filtered by severity and service dependency graph, distributed traces showing latency degradation and error paths, and change events from the prior 24–72 hours.](https://stackgen.com/blog/automate-incident-rca-ai-sre)
2. **Hypothesize:** The agent generates a ranked list of candidate root causes, each linked to specific supporting evidence such as log lines, stack trace frames, or commits.[Evidence-first prompting requires every hypothesis to cite the exact log line, stack frame, or commit that supports it, which prevents plausible but baseless fabrications.](https://howdy.com/blog/ai-native-debugging-framework)
3. **Query:** Specialist sub-agents run targeted queries through MCP tool interfaces. Log agents use file listing, content retrieval, and pattern search. Metric agents use time-series loading and visualization.[Accurate investigation depends on retrieving the narrow slice of logs, traces, recent deploys, infrastructure state, and ownership context that matters for the specific alert, instead of filling a context window with large generic data volumes.](https://metoro.io/blog/ai-tools-for-automated-alert-investigation)
4. **Evaluate:** A supervisor agent performs cross-modal correlation, checks for hallucinated dependencies or missed evidence, and produces a root-cause hypothesis with a confidence score.[Root cause determination occurs once the top hypothesis clears a confidence threshold of 80–90%.](https://stackgen.com/blog/automate-incident-rca-ai-sre)
5. **Verify:** The verifier agent issues targeted queries to observability tools to confirm or reject the hypothesis against hard evidence from live data.[A Validator Agent queries observability tools, including metrics, logs, traces, and cloud APIs, to confirm or reject root-cause hypotheses using hard evidence from the data rather than static runbooks.](https://dzone.com/articles/agentic-ai-sre-copilot-incident-response) Struct's Incident Tracker runs an approximately one-minute automated verification loop against observability data to confirm an incident is actually resolved.
6. **Report:** The agent posts a structured report to Slack with the confirmed root cause, evidence trail, affected services, suggested fix, and a link to the dynamically generated dashboard. Low-confidence findings route to human review automatically.


## Reference Architecture for Closed-Loop Incident Verification


The reference architecture for agentic on-call RCA layers three components: an orchestration framework, a tool protocol, and the observability stack. LangGraph manages stateful multi-agent workflows, maintains the investigation context across steps, and handles conditional branching when a hypothesis is rejected and a new one must be generated. MCP (Model Context Protocol) provides the standardized tool interface through which agents query Datadog metrics, pull CloudWatch logs, fetch Sentry issues, and retrieve GitHub deploy history without custom integration code per tool.


[Struct connects to Datadog metrics, logs, and traces as primary inputs while adding cross-stack investigation into Sentry, GitHub, Cloud logging, and other tools.](https://struct.ai/blog/struct-vs-datadog) The observability stack stays in place as the data source. Struct sits on top as an investigation layer, querying existing Datadog, Prometheus, Grafana, Sentry, and cloud logging infrastructure through authenticated integrations.


[Closed-loop incident resolution verification depends on correlation keys such as trace_id so that post-action checks can automatically tie an alert, agent decision, and downstream recovery signals together without manual timestamp guessing or tab switching.](https://openobserve.ai/blog/logs-traces-metrics-correlation) OpenTelemetry-based trace context propagation lets a single distributed trace span the application, the agent loop, tool executions, and downstream MCP servers. This span enables end-to-end verification of agent actions against observability data.


## Parallel Hypothesis Management, Verification, and Evidence Trails


[LATS-RCA maintains multiple candidate root causes in parallel during search and incrementally gathers evidence from logs and metrics, achieving 91.3% accuracy on the LO2 benchmark.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03505) Struct's hypothesis manager follows the same parallel-maintenance pattern. Multiple hypotheses remain active until evidence eliminates them, which prevents premature convergence on a plausible but incorrect cause.


The verifier operates as a distinct agent from the investigation agents. Investigation agents gather and correlate evidence. The verifier confirms that the proposed root cause actually explains the observed telemetry and, after a fix is applied, that the observability signals have returned to baseline.[GAMAR's Verifier Agent enforces an Adversarial Validation Protocol through counterfactual reasoning and achieves an average F1-score of 88.4%.](https://augmentcode.com/guides/root-cause-analysis-ai-agents)


Every conclusion in the evidence trail links to the specific log line, metric data point, trace span, or commit that supports it.[Capturing the exact JSON payloads, latency, and status of each tool invocation in an agent run enables explanation of why an RCA agent reached a specific conclusion and supports evidence verification.](https://mastra.ai/articles/agent-systems) This trail makes the investigation auditable and reproducible for post-mortems.


## Human Escalation Gates and Safe Remediation


Agentic RCA systems enforce human oversight through structured escalation gates, not optional checkpoints.[Human-in-the-loop governance for agentic RCA systems enforces decision ownership, verification gates, and constraints through RBAC, time-bounded credentials, audit logs, and an autonomy ladder progressing from assist to recommend, approve, execute, and learn stages.](https://rootly.com/ai-sre-guide/concepts)


Struct's permission model separates investigation from remediation. Investigation agents read telemetry and generate hypotheses autonomously. Remediation actions such as rollbacks, scaling changes, and pod restarts require explicit engineer approval via Slack command before execution.[Human approval gates mandate engineer sign-off before any fix is merged and before any incident is closed, regardless of the AI's reported confidence score.](https://howdy.com/blog/ai-native-debugging-framework)


This separation makes on-call rotations safe for junior engineers. Struct provides a fully contextualized starting point for every alert, including blast radius, root cause hypothesis, evidence trail, and suggested fix. A new hire can assess the situation and approve or escalate without relying on years of tribal knowledge about the system.


[See human escalation gates in action](https://cal.com/deepanm/struct-demo) in a live demo of agentic RCA.


## Side-by-Side Timeline: Manual vs Agentic with Datadog and GitHub


This timeline comparison shows where the 40-minute time savings appears, specifically the removed handoffs between Datadog, GitHub, and other tools. Manual investigation forces the engineer to rebuild context at every step, while the agentic path keeps context unified and runs queries in parallel.


**Manual path (45 minutes):** At 3:02 AM, a P1 alert fires in PagerDuty. The on-call engineer acknowledges at 3:05 AM, opens Datadog, and begins scanning dashboards for the anomaly window. By 3:15 AM, they have identified a latency spike in the payments service but have not yet correlated it to a cause. They pivot to Sentry at 3:18 AM, find a spike in database timeout exceptions, and begin manually searching CloudWatch logs for the correlation ID. At 3:28 AM, they find the relevant log lines. They open GitHub at 3:35 AM and scan recent deploys. At 3:42 AM, they identify a migration that ran at 2:58 AM as the likely cause. They propose a rollback at 3:47 AM. Total time to root cause: 45 minutes.


**Agentic path (5 minutes):** At 3:02 AM, the alert fires. Struct begins observation immediately. By 3:04 AM, it has ingested Datadog metrics, correlated the latency spike to database timeout exceptions in Sentry, retrieved the matching CloudWatch log lines by trace ID, and identified the 2:58 AM migration in GitHub deploy history.[Struct ingests Sentry issues the moment they fire and correlates them with Datadog metrics, cloud infrastructure, GitHub deploy history, logs, traces, and other tools to produce a cited root-cause hypothesis.](https://struct.ai/blog/struct-vs-sentry-seer) At 3:07 AM, the engineer opens Slack to find the root cause, evidence trail, and a suggested rollback already posted. Time to root cause: 5 minutes.


## How Agentic RCA Fits Existing Engineering Operations


Agentic RCA plugs into the tools engineering teams already use every day. Struct listens to designated Slack channels or PagerDuty alerts, triggers investigations automatically, and posts results back to the same thread. No new incident management platform is required.[Struct auto-dedupes related alerts with no configuration and runs one investigation per real incident.](https://struct.ai/blog/struct-vs-datadog)


The DORA metrics impact is direct. Faster root cause identification reduces MTTR. Automated deduplication reduces alert noise and the cognitive load that drives senior-engineer burnout.[The time savings described in Arcana's case study flow directly into product development, improving deployment frequency and change failure rate recovery time.](https://struct.ai/blog/struct-vs-datadog)


## Common Pitfalls in Agentic RCA and How to Avoid Them


Three failure modes account for most underperforming agentic RCA deployments, and each one maps to a different layer of the investigation stack. At the data layer, weak or absent telemetry starves the system of the signals it needs. At the knowledge layer, stale runbooks mislead the hypothesis engine. At the verification layer, skipping confirmation checks creates a false sense of resolution.


- **Weak or absent telemetry:** Agentic RCA depends on the quality of the data it queries. Teams without trace IDs in logs, without structured log formats, or without alerting triggers configured receive low-confidence or unhelpful investigations. The minimum viable stack is Sentry or an equivalent exception tracker, a metrics platform such as Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana, cloud logs such as CloudWatch, GCP Logging, or Azure, and a code repository with deploy history.
- **Stale runbooks:**[A 2026 guide on AI root cause analysis identifies stale runbooks as a recurring failure mode in AI RCA tools.](https://coralogix.com/ai-blog/ai-root-cause-analysis) Runbooks that do not reflect current service topology or alert semantics produce misleading hypotheses. Treat runbook updates as part of every post-mortem action item.
- **Skipping the verification step:**[R2Act analysis of 302 quality-audited Kubernetes incidents found that even when root-cause service accuracy reaches 91.4%–99.7%, recovery validity remains only 36.8%–60.3%, which highlights the diagnosis-to-recovery gap.](https://augmentcode.com/guides/root-cause-analysis-ai-agents) Confirming a root cause differs from confirming resolution. Always run the verifier against post-fix observability data before closing an incident.

Teams measure agentic RCA effectiveness through MTTR reduction, investigation recurrence rate, and the ratio of automated to manual investigations.[A practical RCA evaluation framework tracks MTTR, RCA confidence, false positive and false negative rates, and multi-incident reproducibility to measure progress beyond single incidents.](https://suhasbhairav.com/blog/automated-root-cause-analysis-rca-via-agentic-data-mining) Struct's Incident Tracker provides the closed-loop verification data needed to populate these metrics automatically, confirming resolution against observability data instead of relying on engineer self-reporting.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What minimum tooling maturity is required for agentic on-call root cause analysis?


The minimum viable stack requires a structured alerting trigger such as a Slack channel, PagerDuty, or Sentry, at least one observability platform with queryable logs or metrics such as Datadog, Prometheus, CloudWatch, GCP Logging, or Grafana, and a code repository with deploy history such as GitHub. Struct connects to all three categories and begins producing investigations immediately after authentication. Teams without trace IDs in logs or without structured log formats receive lower-confidence investigations. The practical floor is a team already using Sentry or an equivalent exception tracker alongside cloud logs and a metrics platform. Setup takes under 10 minutes.


### How does incident resolution verification handle security and compliance?


Struct is[SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant](https://trust.struct.ai/) , with the full trust posture documented at trust.struct.ai. Logs and telemetry are accessed and processed ephemerally, and they are not stored beyond the investigation window. RBAC controls which integrations each user can query and which remediation actions require approval. Audit logs capture every agent action, tool invocation, and hypothesis generated, which provides the immutable evidence trail required for compliance reviews. Teams with strict requirements that prohibit any data leaving their VPC should evaluate whether on-premise deployment options fit their constraints before onboarding.


### Can junior engineers safely participate in agentic RCA workflows?


Junior engineers can safely participate when human escalation gates control remediation. The human escalation gate model is designed to make on-call participation safe for engineers without deep systemic context. Struct completes the first-pass investigation automatically, including blast radius, root cause hypothesis, evidence trail, and suggested fix, before the engineer engages. The junior engineer reviews a structured summary rather than starting from a blank Datadog dashboard at 3 AM. Remediation actions require explicit approval, so no change executes without a human decision. Custom runbooks encode the team's specific operational procedures, giving newer engineers the same starting context a senior engineer would have built from memory.


### How is resolution automatically confirmed against observability data?


Struct's Incident Tracker runs an approximately one-minute automated verification loop after a fix is applied. The verifier agent re-queries the same observability signals that triggered the original alert, including error rates, latency percentiles, exception counts, and relevant log patterns, and compares current values against the pre-incident baseline. If the signals have returned to baseline and no new anomalies are detected, the incident is marked resolved with a timestamped evidence record. If signals remain elevated or new anomalies appear, the incident stays open and the engineer is notified. This closed-loop model, called incident resolution verification, removes the common failure mode of closing incidents based on engineer assumption rather than confirmed observability data.
